clearingRule: source-brand-inline-svg clears ONLY on OUTPUT PROOF, evaluated by evaluateBrandOutputProof (src/release/brand-scan.ts) over a build's OWN measurements. (a) brand.bake.residual.unexplainedAfter must be EMPTY — that array is re-derived by RE-READING the mutated page files from disk after the rewrite, never from the in-memory objects the rewrite produced, so it means: every brand-carrying host still in the built app's IR is covered by an explicit PRESERVE. (b) when nothing is preserved, the RENDERED output must agree — the exported route-HTML census AND the RSC flight census (both .txt flight files and the self.__next_f.push chunks inlined in each HTML) must be zero. (c) and when the build carries a POST-HYDRATION census (the QA run's brandSurfaceCensusHydrated, taken over the live DOM of every route in Chromium), that must be zero too; a build with no hydrated census reports the axis as UNMEASURED rather than counting it clean. A decision alone never clears it; a REPLACE the resolver REFUSED, or one the census still sees, leaves it standing with a statusNote saying exactly that. CORRECTION (this pass): WHAT cleared a build is now separated from WHETHER the rule accepted it. BrandOutputProof.clearedBy is 'output-proof' when every MEASURED axis is zero — the only value that earns status=resolved — and 'preserve-acceptance' when the IR is explained only because a host was explicitly PRESERVED while the output is NOT clean. A preserve-acceptance build lands as status='accepted-limitation', which releaseBlockers() STILL COUNTS, so PRESERVE-everything is not a path to PRODUCTION_READY and the requirement never reads 'resolved' while the source mark is shipping. Severity and its basis text were not touched.

limitations: CORRECTED — the previous text of this limitation was FALSE. It asserted, with a named grep as its evidence, that an source logo 'does not exist in ANY accepted template in this repo'. Running this phase's own scanner over data/nextjs.org/recon-templates/2026-08-19T07-12-35-732Z/app returns 160 image-logo hosts over 40 routes on two source logotype files. The surface now runs on that real lineage (smoke-brand-assets §5e, two real `next build`s). What remains true and narrower: linear.app, stripe.com and domainchecker.co.kr ship no source logo, so the REFUSAL paths on that surface (a text-only REPLACE on an , REMOVE on an ) are still exercised only on the synthetic fixture.

An icon SPRITE host (a host that defines <symbol>s) refuses whole-host REPLACE/REMOVE. Only its brand-named symbol ids are resolvable. A brand svg-aria-label or svg-text ON a sprite host can therefore be cleared only by an explicit PRESERVE with a recorded reason — it is an honest standing requirement otherwise. On the accepted linear template no such case exists (the sprite's brand surfaces are all symbol ids), so this refusal path is exercised only on the fixture.

Arbitrary SVG <path> geometry that draws the source mark without naming the brand anywhere is NOT detected and NOT resolved. This is a detection limit, not a resolver limit, and it is out of scope by the settled 'no SVG path editor' constraint. A source logo that is pure unlabelled path data will pass every axis of the clearing rule while still being the source's mark.

REMOVE on an host is refused unconditionally (the element carries layout the surrounding flex/grid depends on). The operator must REPLACE. There is no structural-safety analysis that would let a genuinely safe removal through.

dynamic-template-content is UNOWNED: no artifact records brand inside dynamically-mounted region content separately from its host route, so brand carried only by a portal/overlay region is not separately censused.

The clearing rule's post-hydration axis is optional by construction: a production build that carries no report/qa.json (or an older one without brandSurfaceCensusHydrated) clears on the two byte-level axes alone, with the detail string saying 'post-hydration brand surfaces=not measured'. This is deliberate — an unmeasured axis must not be scored as clean — but it does mean an operator reading only `status: resolved` should read the statusNote to know how many axes proved it.

The persisted requirements.json of the real wr28-brand-assets project still shows the TWO-axis statusNote, because its build (2026-08-27T12-36-06-105Z) predates the hydrated census. I did NOT rewrite that historical build's artifacts. I re-measured the third axis on that exact package myself (8/8 routes, 0 brand surfaces, 0 divergent routes) and proved collectRequirements consumes it, over a scratch copy — see verification.collectPlumbingOnRealLineage. The next real build of that project will persist all three axes.

The canary's `next build`s run on a 1-ROUTE copy of the accepted template (route-map filtered to '/'), to keep each build at ~2.5 s. The 8-route proof is the real wr28-brand-assets lineage, not the canary.

brandSurfaceCensus and brandSurfaceCensusHydrated remain REPORTED, never gated, inside production QA. The gate that consumes them is the release layer's evaluateBrandOutputProof. This preserves the Task-27 stance that a blanket zero-equality assertion over a brand string count is not an honest gate.

DETECTION IS STILL TOKEN-DERIVED. Tokens are the host label plus the brand name the source declares in its own recurring title suffix. A brand string derivable from neither — an alternate spelling, a logotype with no accessible name, a site that does not append its name to its titles — raises NOTHING, and because the blocker's trigger is brandCarryingHostCount > 0 the requirement is then absent rather than merely small. Measured: this is exactly what happened on domainchecker.co.kr before the widening (794 inline SVGs, 0 hosts, no requirement, while aria-label="도메인체커 홈" shipped). The widening closes that case; it does not close the class. Mitigation, not a fix: src/release/collect.ts now emits a warning whenever a template has inline-SVG entries and ZERO detected brand hosts, so the zero is stated rather than silent.

THE DECLARED-NAME WIDENING CAN OVER-INCLUDE. It is a brand-NAME match, not a brand-MARK match: on nextjs.org it takes the count from 160 to 190 by catching alt/aria-label prose that merely mentions the product ('Hydration error message improved in Next.js 15'). Those are genuine source-brand mentions and each still needs an operator decision, but an operator should expect the count to include prose mentions, not only marks. Over-inclusion is the deliberate direction: under-detection makes a blocker vanish, over-detection only makes it longer.

PRESERVE NOW LANDS AS accepted-limitation, WHICH STILL BLOCKS — so there is no path from a PRESERVE decision to PRODUCTION_READY. The consequence to be aware of is the mirror image: a lineage where the operator legitimately may ship a source mark (a licensed placement, an icon sprite whose brand aria-label cannot be safely rewritten) can no longer reach a clean release state through this kind at all — it stays blocked, visibly, with the reason recorded. That is intended under the policy basis 'visible source-brand content must be 0', but it means PRESERVE is an acknowledgement, never a resolution.

ATTRIBUTE-VALUE PROSE IS UNOWNED AND UNCOUNTED. Measured in this phase's own proof build: data/linear.app/production-builds/2026-08-27T12-36-06-105Z/package/site/index.html ships placeholder="Tell Linear what to do next…" twice (title=0, value=0 on the same package). `placeholder` is not in BRAND_SURFACES, no detector raises it, and no census axis counts it — censusServedHtml strips tags before reading visible text, so an attribute value never reaches it. It is now DECLARED in the bake report (SURFACES_NOT_RESOLVED['attribute-value-text']) and asserted by a check, so the gap is recorded rather than silent — but a zero census still does NOT mean this class is clean.

STALE-PROOF NUANCE (verified NOT a gate hole, recorded anyway): readBrandOutputProof reads the current production artifact's report regardless of freshness, so a requirement can read its status from a build that predates a later authored.brand change. It cannot reach PRODUCTION_READY that way — deriveReleaseState additionally requires stageStatus.production.status==='fresh', and authored.brand is folded into the production stage's inputsHash, so any decision change stales the stage.

SCOPE OF THIS CORRECTION PASS: I ran typecheck plus seven suites (brand-assets, release, production, content-injection, assets, seo, theme), not all 20, so no full-program regression total is stated here. Other agents were running in parallel under the same mutex. Zero mutating git operations; nothing was written under data/ except the suites' own pid-scoped fixture roots, which they delete.
